newsitem.title: USA: Investors eagerly await new U.S. corporate debt.
newsitem.headline: Investors eagerly await new U.S. corporate debt.

text.p: Corporate bond issuance is expected to maintain a healthy pace as U.S. Treasury yields spur issuers to tap the market and eager investors scoop up the deals, dealers said.
"There are a few names in the market and so far I'm hearing they may be upped in size to meet investor demand," said one syndicate source.
WMX Technologies is expected to price $200 million in 10-year debt via Merrill Lynch & Co but market sources said the deal may have to be upped in size to meet demand.
"The WMX issue is expected to come at $200 million but already I hear the deal is growing," another syndicate source said.
In other issues, Petronas' $1.0 billion two-part debt offering may also have to be boosted higher to accommodate hungry investors, sources said.
The deal currently is expected to consist of $500 million in five-year debt and $500 million in 10-year debt, dealers said.

Lower financing rates and a rapidly approaching end to the calendar year should push issuance to the forefront now as upcoming holidays, coupled with thinly staffed desks, make it virtually impossible to structure new deals, dealers said.
"We're in a very positive issuing environment," said one syndicate source. "Investors scooping up the paper as it comes to market."
Among other foreign issues, Banco Santander is expected to price $150 million in 10-year subordinated yankee notes.
Banco Nationale de Paris is expected to tap the market with $350 million in 10-year subordinated yankee debt via Salomon Brothers in early October.
Brazil is also expected to tap the market with a five-year or ten-year global issue, sources said.
In high-yield issues, Goss Graphic Systems is expected to issue $225 million in B2/B-rated senior subordianted notes due 2006 via CS First Boston.
Paging Network Inc is expected to price $350 million in 144A senior subordinated notes due 2008 via Goldman Sachs.
In the government market, the U.S. Treasury 30-year bond is up 3/32 at 99-19/32 to yield 6.78 percent.
